question: How likely is the 'solar plant west davidport' (matching the name regardless of case) to be down when we need it? Give me its system unavailability score, just the number, to four decimal points.
gold_sql:
SELECT ROUND(CAST(om."mttrh" / (om."mtbfh" + om."mttrh") AS numeric), 4)
FROM operational_metrics om
JOIN plant_record pr ON om."snapops" = pr."snapkey"
JOIN plants p ON pr."sitetie" = p."sitekey"
WHERE LOWER(p."sitelabel") = 'solar plant west davidport'
LIMIT 1;

question: I need to know the financial hit from plants with recurring warranty issues—the ones whose warranty status is 'claimed' and have had three or more claims logged against them. Can you figure out the total lifetime revenue loss for them, but only count ones where we know their go-live date and degradation? Just assume they all have 15 years left, produce 500,000 kwh a year, and we sell the power at 12 cents. Give me the grand total.
gold_sql:
WITH warranty_risk_plants AS (
    SELECT 
        p."sitekey",
        p."goliveon"
    FROM plants p
    WHERE LOWER(p."warrstate") = 'claimed' AND p."warrclaims" > 2
),
adr_calcs AS (
    SELECT
        wrp."sitekey",
        (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'efficiency' ->> 'cumulative_deg_pct')::real / NULLIF(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM AGE(NOW(), wrp."goliveon")), 0) AS adr
    FROM warranty_risk_plants wrp
    JOIN plant_record pr ON wrp."sitekey" = pr."sitetie"
    JOIN electrical_performance ep ON pr."snapkey" = ep."snaplink"
    WHERE (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'efficiency' ->> 'cumulative_deg_pct') IS NOT NULL AND wrp."goliveon" IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
    SUM(ac.adr * 500000 * 0.12 * 15) AS total_lifetime_revenue_loss
FROM adr_calcs ac;

question: If we could magically cool the panels for snapshot pv945724 down to 25 degrees celsius, what would its power output be? Give me the temperature-corrected performance in watts, with two decimal points.
gold_sql:
WITH thermal_loss AS (
    SELECT
        (((env_snapshot -> 'temperatures' ->> 'cell_temp_c')::real - 25) * ABS(pm.tempcoeff)) AS loss_factor,
        (elec_perf_snapshot -> 'power' ->> 'power_now_w')::real AS actual_power
    FROM electrical_performance ep
    JOIN plant_record pr ON ep.snaplink = pr.snapkey
    JOIN plants p ON pr.sitetie = p.sitekey
    JOIN panel_models pm ON p.modhook = pm.modkey
    JOIN environmental_conditions ec ON pr.snapkey = ec.snapref
    WHERE LOWER(ep.snaplink) = 'pv945724'
)
SELECT ROUND(CAST(actual_power / (1 - loss_factor) AS numeric), 2)
FROM thermal_loss;

question: For the maintenance event pv937101, did the repair cost more than the revenue we lost during the downtime? To figure that out, you'll have to clean up the revenue loss text by stripping out any '$' or ',' characters. Tell me the maintenance cost to revenue impact ratio, just the number, rounded to two decimals.

How many of our plants are real lemons, both losing more than a quarter of their potential power and being offline for more than one day out of every twenty? Make sure you only use records that have all the numbers needed for the math. Just give me the total count.
gold_sql:
WITH asset_kpis AS (
    SELECT 
        p.sitekey,
        ((ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'energy_yield' ->> 'specific_yield_kwh_kw')::real / ((ec.env_snapshot -> 'irradiance' ->> 'poa_irr_w_m2')::real / 1000)) AS performance_ratio,
        (1 - (om.mttrh / (om.mtbfh + om.mttrh))) AS system_availability
    FROM plants p
    JOIN plant_record pr ON p.sitekey = pr.sitetie
    JOIN electrical_performance ep ON pr.snapkey = ep.snaplink
    JOIN environmental_conditions ec ON pr.snapkey = ec.snapref
    JOIN operational_metrics om ON pr.snapkey = om.snapops
    WHERE 
        (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'energy_yield' ->> 'specific_yield_kwh_kw') IS NOT NULL
        AND (ec.env_snapshot -> 'irradiance' ->> 'poa_irr_w_m2') IS NOT NULL
        AND (ec.env_snapshot -> 'irradiance' ->> 'poa_irr_w_m2')::real > 0
        AND om.mttrh IS NOT NULL AND om.mtbfh IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT sitekey)
FROM asset_kpis
WHERE performance_ratio < 0.75 AND system_availability < 0.95;

question: Using the latest data for each plant, find the one that costs the most to run for its size, and tell me how much power it loses internally. I need the system power loss ratio for whichever plant has the biggest operational expenditure index. Give me the number to 4 decimal places, and only consider plants and snapshots with all the necessary and valid data to make the calculation crash-proof.
gold_sql:
WITH latest_snapshots AS (
    SELECT sitetie, MAX(snapts) as max_ts
    FROM plant_record
    GROUP BY sitetie
),
plant_kpis AS (
    SELECT
        p.sitekey,
        (om.maintcost + om.cleancost + om.replcost) / NULLIF(p.cap_mw * 1000, 0) AS oei,
        (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'power' ->> 'power_loss_w')::numeric / NULLIF(((ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'power' ->> 'power_now_w')::numeric + (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'power' ->> 'power_loss_w')::numeric), 0) AS system_power_loss_ratio
    FROM plants p
    JOIN plant_record pr ON p.sitekey = pr.sitetie
    JOIN latest_snapshots ls ON pr.sitetie = ls.sitetie AND pr.snapts = ls.max_ts
    JOIN operational_metrics om ON pr.snapkey = om.snapops
    JOIN electrical_performance ep ON pr.snapkey = ep.snaplink
    WHERE p.cap_mw IS NOT NULL AND p.cap_mw > 0
      AND (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'power' ->> 'power_now_w') IS NOT NULL
      AND (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'power' ->> 'power_loss_w') IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT ROUND(CAST(system_power_loss_ratio AS numeric), 4)
FROM plant_kpis
WHERE oei IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY oei DESC
LIMIT 1;

question: When our panel busbars are as corroded as they can get, how much does the quality drop? Calculate the average fill factor degradation for all panels in the worst category for corrosion (regardless of case), but only use data where we have both a before and after fill factor. Give me the result to 3 decimal places.
gold_sql:
SELECT 
    ROUND(CAST(AVG((ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'iv_curve' ->> 'fill_factor_initial')::real - (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'iv_curve' ->> 'fill_factor_now')::real) AS numeric), 3)
FROM electrical_performance ep
JOIN mechanical_condition mc ON ep.snaplink = mc.snapmk
WHERE LOWER(mc.mech_health_snapshot -> 'module_surface' ->> 'busbar_corrosion') = 'severe'
  AND (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'iv_curve' ->> 'fill_factor_initial') IS NOT NULL 
  AND (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'iv_curve' ->> 'fill_factor_now') IS NOT NULL;

question: When a plant with hjt panels breaks, what's the average cost to fix it? Calculate the mean repair cost for those plants (matching 'hjt' regardless of case), assuming they've been running for two years straight and have a valid, positive mtbf record. Give me the final number, rounded to a whole dollar.
gold_sql:
SELECT 
    ROUND(CAST(AVG(om.maintcost / (17520 / om.mtbfh)) AS numeric))
FROM operational_metrics om
JOIN plant_record pr ON om.snapops = pr.snapkey
JOIN plants p ON pr.sitetie = p.sitekey
JOIN panel_models pm ON p.modhook = pm.modkey
WHERE LOWER(pm.pnlkind) = 'hjt' 
  AND om.mtbfh IS NOT NULL 
  AND om.mtbfh > 0;

question: When our electrical systems fail, how much money do we lose? Add up all the revenue loss from every incident with an 'electrical integrity failure', making sure to strip the dollar signs and commas from the text to get the total.
gold_sql:
SELECT SUM(REPLACE(REPLACE(om.revloss, '$', ''), ',', '')::numeric)
FROM operational_metrics om
JOIN mechanical_condition mc ON om.snapops = mc.snapmk
WHERE LOWER(mc.mech_health_snapshot -> 'electrical_integrity' ->> 'grounding_status') = 'failed'
OR LOWER(mc.mech_health_snapshot->'electrical_integrity'->>'bypass_diode_status') != 'normal';

question: After accounting for all the internal power drains, what's the actual juice each plant is sending to the grid right now? Only using snapshots where we know both the power loss and current output, and their combined total isn't zero, give me a list of plant names and their latest effective power output, rounded to two decimal places, with the most powerful plant at the top.
gold_sql:
WITH latest_snapshots AS (
    SELECT sitetie, MAX(snapts) as max_ts
    FROM plant_record
    GROUP BY sitetie
),
loss_ratio AS (
    SELECT 
        pr.sitetie,
        (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'power' ->> 'power_loss_w')::numeric / 
            NULLIF(((ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'power' ->> 'power_now_w')::numeric + 
            (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'power' ->> 'power_loss_w')::numeric), 0) AS splr,
        (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'power' ->> 'power_now_w')::numeric + (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'power' ->> 'power_loss_w')::numeric AS gross_power
    FROM electrical_performance ep
    JOIN plant_record pr ON ep.snaplink = pr.snapkey
    JOIN latest_snapshots ls ON pr.sitetie = ls.sitetie AND pr.snapts = ls.max_ts
    WHERE (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'power' ->> 'power_loss_w') IS NOT NULL 
      AND (ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'power' ->> 'power_now_w') IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
    p.sitelabel,
    ROUND(CAST(lr.gross_power * (1 - lr.splr) AS numeric), 2) AS effective_power
FROM plants p
JOIN loss_ratio lr ON p.sitekey = lr.sitetie
ORDER BY effective_power DESC;

question: For the plants that are aging terribly—meaning their performance drops by more than 0.5% a year—how long does it typically take to fix them? I need the average mean-time-to-repair for these 'accelerated aging assets'. The age calculation needs to be safe for new plants. Give me the answer in hours, rounded to two decimal places.
gold_sql:
WITH accelerated_aging AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT p.sitekey
    FROM plants p
    JOIN plant_record pr ON p.sitekey = pr.sitetie
    JOIN electrical_performance ep ON pr.snapkey = ep.snaplink
    JOIN mechanical_condition mc ON pr.snapkey = mc.snapmk
    WHERE 
        -- Major Module Degradation criteria
        LOWER(mc.mech_health_snapshot -> 'module_surface' ->> 'busbar_corrosion') = 'severe' AND
        LOWER(mc.mech_health_snapshot -> 'module_surface' ->> 'delamination_status') = 'major' AND
        (mc.mech_health_snapshot -> 'module_surface' ->> 'microcrack_count')::integer > 5 AND
        -- High Annual Degradation Rate criteria
        p.goliveon IS NOT NULL AND
        ((ep.elec_perf_snapshot -> 'efficiency' ->> 'cumulative_deg_pct')::real / NULLIF(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM AGE(NOW(), p.goliveon)), 0)) > 0.5
)
SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(om.mttrh) AS numeric), 2)
FROM operational_metrics om
JOIN plant_record pr ON om.snapops = pr.snapkey
WHERE pr.sitetie IN (SELECT sitekey FROM accelerated_aging);

question: Let's get a financial forecast for our worst panels, the ones that degrade so fast they'll lose over 14% of their power in 20 years. What's the total projected revenue loss over their remaining 15-year lifespan? Base the calculation on a standard 400,000 mwh annual output and a sale price of $50 per mwh.
gold_sql:
WITH high_degradation_models AS (
    SELECT "modkey", "degyrrate" FROM panel_models WHERE "degyrrate" > 0.7
), plant_adr AS (
    SELECT 
        p."sitekey", 
        hdm.degyrrate / 100 AS adr
    FROM plants p
    JOIN high_degradation_models hdm ON p."modhook" = hdm."modkey"
)
SELECT 
    SUM(pa.adr * 400000 * 50 * 15)
FROM plant_adr pa;

question: How much are the different types of panels losing their voltage punch over time? I need you to group by the panel technology, making sure to ignore case, and then figure out the average voltage degradation factor for each. But hey, only use data where we actually have a valid 'before' and 'after' voltage to compare, and make sure the starting voltage isn't zero. List the panel types and their average voltage loss, with the worst ones first.
gold_sql:
SELECT 
    LOWER(pm."pnlkind") as pnlkind,
    AVG((CAST(ep.elec_perf_snapshot->'iv_curve'->>'vmp_initial_v' AS REAL) - CAST(ep.elec_perf_snapshot->'iv_curve'->>'vmp_now_v' AS REAL)) / CAST(ep.elec_perf_snapshot->'iv_curve'->>'vmp_initial_v' AS REAL))
FROM electrical_performance ep
JOIN plant_record pr ON ep."snaplink" = pr."snapkey"
JOIN plants p ON pr."sitetie" = p."sitekey"
JOIN panel_models pm ON p."modhook" = pm."modkey"
WHERE 
    ep.elec_perf_snapshot->'iv_curve'->>'vmp_initial_v' IS NOT NULL 
    AND ep.elec_perf_snapshot->'iv_curve'->>'vmp_now_v' IS NOT NULL
    AND CAST(ep.elec_perf_snapshot->'iv_curve'->>'vmp_initial_v' AS REAL) > 0
GROUP BY LOWER(pm."pnlkind")
ORDER BY AVG((CAST(ep.elec_perf_snapshot->'iv_curve'->>'vmp_initial_v' AS REAL) - CAST(ep.elec_perf_snapshot->'iv_curve'->>'vmp_now_v' AS REAL)) / CAST(ep.elec_perf_snapshot->'iv_curve'->>'vmp_initial_v' AS REAL)) DESC;

question: For the machines that are down more than one day in a 20-day period, what's the average price tag on a single repair? To calculate the mean repair cost, you'll need to figure out how long each machine has been running. Only use data where the mtbf and service time are positive.
gold_sql:
WITH chronic_downtime_assets AS (
    SELECT 
        snapops
    FROM operational_metrics
    WHERE (1 - (mttrh / (mtbfh + mttrh))) < 0.95 AND mttrh IS NOT NULL AND mtbfh IS NOT NULL AND (mtbfh + mttrh) > 0
), time_in_service AS (
    SELECT
        pr.snapkey,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (pr.snapts - p.goliveon))/3600 AS total_hours
    FROM plant_record pr
    JOIN plants p on pr.sitetie = p.sitekey
)
SELECT 
    AVG(om.maintcost / (tis.total_hours / om.mtbfh))
FROM operational_metrics om
JOIN time_in_service tis ON om.snapops = tis.snapkey
WHERE om.snapops IN (SELECT snapops FROM chronic_downtime_assets) AND tis.total_hours > 0 AND om.mtbfh > 0;

question: How many of our plants have a major electrical issue right now? I'm talking about situations where the grounding is shot or the bypass diodes are not running in their normal state. FROM mechanical_condition mc
JOIN plant_record pr ON mc.snapmk = pr.snapkey
WHERE 
    LOWER(mc.mech_health_snapshot->'electrical_integrity'->>'grounding_status') = 'failed'
    OR LOWER(mc.mech_health_snapshot->'electrical_integrity'->>'bypass_diode_status') != 'normal';

question: After accounting for all the power being lost inside the system, what was the actual usable power output for snapshot 'pv945724'? Give me the final number in watts.
gold_sql:
WITH loss_ratio AS (
    SELECT 
        CAST(elec_perf_snapshot->'power'->>'power_loss_w' AS REAL) / 
        (CAST(elec_perf_snapshot->'power'->>'power_now_w' AS REAL) + CAST(elec_perf_snapshot->'power'->>'power_loss_w' AS REAL)) as r_loss,
        CAST(elec_perf_snapshot->'power'->>'power_now_w' AS REAL) + CAST(elec_perf_snapshot->'power'->>'power_loss_w' AS REAL) as p_gross
    FROM electrical_performance
    WHERE snaplink = 'PV945724'
)
SELECT 
    lr.p_gross * (1 - lr.r_loss)
FROM loss_ratio lr;

question: For the panels specifically made by longi (regardless of case), how much has their current output dropped on average? To get a good average, please only use records where you have a valid, positive starting current to compare against. Calculate the mean current degradation factor across all of them.
gold_sql:
SELECT 
    AVG((CAST(ep.elec_perf_snapshot->'iv_curve'->>'imp_initial_a' AS REAL) - CAST(ep.elec_perf_snapshot->'iv_curve'->>'imp_now_a' AS REAL)) / CAST(ep.elec_perf_snapshot->'iv_curve'->>'imp_initial_a' AS REAL))
FROM electrical_performance ep
JOIN plant_record pr ON ep.snaplink = pr.snapkey
JOIN plants p ON pr.sitetie = p.sitekey
JOIN panel_models pm ON p.modhook = pm.modkey
WHERE 
    LOWER(pm.makertag) = 'longi'
    AND ep.elec_perf_snapshot->'iv_curve'->>'imp_initial_a' IS NOT NULL
    AND ep.elec_perf_snapshot->'iv_curve'->>'imp_now_a' IS NOT NULL
    AND CAST(ep.elec_perf_snapshot->'iv_curve'->>'imp_initial_a' AS REAL) > 0;

question: Let’s check which shows have tons of content across different releases but no written description. Add up their standard content (episodes, clips, etc.) across all tiers, keep only the ones with over 500 total, and no annotations. Show each show’s ID, name, and total volume—sorted by volume, highest first.
gold_sql:
WITH parsed_rollups AS (
  SELECT
    sr.srkeys AS content_key,
    (
      /* Ep_Vol */
      CASE
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Ep_Vol') IS NULL THEN 0
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Ep_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?\s*[kK]$'
          THEN (regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Ep_Vol','[^0-9\.]','','g'))::numeric * 1000
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Ep_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?\s*[mM]$'
          THEN (regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Ep_Vol','[^0-9\.]','','g'))::numeric * 1000000
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Ep_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?\s*[bB]$'
          THEN (regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Ep_Vol','[^0-9\.]','','g'))::numeric * 1000000000
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Ep_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$'
          THEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Ep_Vol')::numeric
        ELSE COALESCE(NULLIF(regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Ep_Vol','[^0-9]','','g'),''),'0')::numeric
      END
      +
      /* Clip_Vol */
      CASE
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Clip_Vol') IS NULL THEN 0
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Clip_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?\s*[kK]$'
          THEN (regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Clip_Vol','[^0-9\.]','','g'))::numeric * 1000
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Clip_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?\s*[mM]$'
          THEN (regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Clip_Vol','[^0-9\.]','','g'))::numeric * 1000000
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Clip_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?\s*[bB]$'
          THEN (regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Clip_Vol','[^0-9\.]','','g'))::numeric * 1000000000
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Clip_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$'

        ELSE COALESCE(NULLIF(regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Clip_Vol','[^0-9]','','g'),''),'0')::numeric
      END
      +
      /* Game_Vol */
      CASE
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Game_Vol') IS NULL THEN 0
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Game_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?\s*[kK]$'
          THEN (regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Game_Vol','[^0-9\.]','','g'))::numeric * 1000
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Game_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?\s*[mM]$'
          THEN (regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Game_Vol','[^0-9\.]','','g'))::numeric * 1000000
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Game_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?\s*[bB]$'
          THEN (regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Game_Vol','[^0-9\.]','','g'))::numeric * 1000000000
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Game_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$'
          THEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Game_Vol')::numeric
        ELSE COALESCE(NULLIF(regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Game_Vol','[^0-9]','','g'),''),'0')::numeric
      END

          THEN (regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Trailer_Vol','[^0-9\.]','','g'))::numeric * 1000000
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Trailer_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?\s*[bB]$'
          THEN (regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Trailer_Vol','[^0-9\.]','','g'))::numeric * 1000000000
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Trailer_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$'
          THEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Trailer_Vol')::numeric
        ELSE COALESCE(NULLIF(regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Trailer_Vol','[^0-9]','','g'),''),'0')::numeric
      END
      +
      /* FilmClip_Vol */
      CASE
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'FilmClip_Vol') IS NULL THEN 0
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'FilmClip_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?\s*[kK]$'
          THEN (regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'FilmClip_Vol','[^0-9\.]','','g'))::numeric * 1000
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'FilmClip_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?\s*[mM]$'
          THEN (regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'FilmClip_Vol','[^0-9\.]','','g'))::numeric * 1000000
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'FilmClip_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?\s*[bB]$'
          THEN (regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'FilmClip_Vol','[^0-9\.]','','g'))::numeric * 1000000000
        WHEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'FilmClip_Vol') ~* '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$'
          THEN (sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'FilmClip_Vol')::numeric
        ELSE COALESCE(NULLIF(regexp_replace(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'FilmClip_Vol','[^0-9]','','g'),''),'0')::numeric
      END
    )::numeric AS std_content_sum
  FROM show_rollups sr
),
agg_per_title AS (
  SELECT
    c.content_key,
    c.content_title,
    SUM(p.std_content_sum) AS total_content_volume
  FROM parsed_rollups p
  JOIN core c ON c.content_key = p.content_key
  GROUP BY c.content_key, c.content_title
),
no_annotation AS (
  SELECT content_key
  FROM core
  WHERE TRIM(COALESCE(annotations, '')) = ''
)
SELECT
  a.content_key,
  a.content_title,
  a.total_content_volume
FROM agg_per_title a
JOIN no_annotation n USING (content_key)
WHERE a.total_content_volume > 500
ORDER BY a.total_content_volume DESC;

question: I want to find shows that show up in three or more different subscription tiers. For each show, can you count how many unique tiers it’s available in? First, keep the ones that are in at least three tiers, and then sort the results from the most widely distributed to the last.
gold_sql: WITH tier_distribution AS ( SELECT srkeys AS content_key, COUNT(DISTINCT srlinks) AS tier_count FROM show_rollups GROUP BY srkeys ) SELECT content_key, tier_count FROM tier_distribution WHERE tier_count >= 3 ORDER BY tier_count DESC;

question: Let’s find out which titles are getting strong user scores even though they don’t have any trailers or clips. I want to look across all content and find the highest user rating among those that don’t offer any visual previews but still include a valid score. Just return that one number, rounded to 2 decimals—it tells us how well these visually sparse titles are performing.
gold_sql: WITH visually_empty_titles AS ( SELECT content_key, content_title, REGEXP_REPLACE(genreclass->>'User_Score', '[^0-9.]', '', 'g')::numeric AS user_score FROM core JOIN content_info USING (content_key) WHERE (mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Film_Clips')::int = 0 AND (mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Clips_Total')::int = 0 AND genreclass->>'User_Score' IS NOT NULL ) SELECT ROUND(MAX(user_score), 2) AS max_rating FROM visually_empty_titles;

question: I want to find out how long it's been since each show got any new updates. For each show, check the most recent update date. But if there's no update info, just use the launch date instead. Then, I’d like to see how many days it's been since that date, and treat that as the staleness score. If a show is available in multiple tiers, take the smallest one. Can you show the show ID and the number of days it's been stale? Finally, sort the list so the stalest shows—that is, the ones that haven't been updated in the longest time—come first.
gold_sql:
WITH content_dates AS (
  SELECT 
    srkeys AS content_key,
    COALESCE(
      CASE 
        WHEN latestadd ~ '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}' THEN TO_DATE(SUBSTRING(latestadd FROM 1 FOR 10), 'YYYY-MM-DD')
        WHEN latestadd ~ '^\d{4}/\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}$' THEN TO_DATE(latestadd, 'YYYY/MM/DD')
        WHEN latestadd ~ '^\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{2}$' THEN TO_DATE(latestadd, 'MM/DD/YY')
        WHEN latestadd ~ '^[A-Za-z]{3,9} \d{1,2}, \d{4}$' THEN TO_DATE(latestadd, 'Mon DD, YYYY')
        ELSE NULL
      END,
      CASE 
        WHEN launchmoment ~ '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}' THEN TO_DATE(SUBSTRING(launchmoment FROM 1 FOR 10), 'YYYY-MM-DD')
        WHEN launchmoment ~ '^\d{4}/\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}$' THEN TO_DATE(launchmoment, 'YYYY/MM/DD')
        WHEN launchmoment ~ '^\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{2}$' THEN TO_DATE(launchmoment, 'MM/DD/YY')
        WHEN launchmoment ~ '^[A-Za-z]{3,9} \d{1,2}, \d{4}$' THEN TO_DATE(launchmoment, 'Mon DD, YYYY')
        ELSE NULL
      END
    ) AS effective_date
  FROM show_rollups
)
SELECT 
  content_key,
  EXTRACT(DAY FROM AGE(CURRENT_DATE, MIN(effective_date))) AS temporal_staleness_index
FROM content_dates
WHERE effective_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY content_key
ORDER BY temporal_staleness_index DESC;

question: How many titles are spread across over six nested genre tags and lean more on short clips, including both general clips and film-related clips, than full-length features?
gold_sql: WITH per_show AS (  SELECT     c.content_key,     regexp_split_to_array(       COALESCE(c.genreclass->>'Hierarchical_Genres', ''),       '[~|]+'     ) AS genres,     COALESCE((NULLIF(ci.mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Clips_Total',''))::int, 0)     + COALESCE((NULLIF(ci.mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Film_Clips',''))::int, 0)       AS short_form_count,     COALESCE((NULLIF(ci.mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Feature_Films',''))::int, 0)       AS feature_count   FROM core c   JOIN content_info ci USING (content_key) ), fragmented AS (   SELECT content_key   FROM per_show   WHERE cardinality(genres) > 6     AND short_form_count > feature_count ) SELECT COUNT(*) AS fragmented_offering_count FROM fragmented;

question: Let’s all find groups of shows that belong to the same franchise. Can you only include franchises that have at least two shows? For each group, can you show me the franchise ID, how many shows it has, and list the show titles? Also, I need to sort the list so that the biggest franchises with the most shows come first.
gold_sql: WITH franchise_titles AS ( SELECT series_id, COUNT(*) AS show_count, STRING_AGG(content_title, ', ') AS titles_in_franchise FROM core WHERE series_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY series_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ) SELECT * FROM franchise_titles ORDER BY show_count DESC;

question: I want to find out how many episodes there are on average in each season for every show. Can you look at shows where we know both the total number of episodes and how many seasons they have. For each one, give me the show ID, how many episodes it has, how many seasons, and the average episodes per season. Please skip anything where the season count is missing or zero. Finally, show the ones with the highest average first.
gold_sql: WITH episode_ratio_calc AS ( SELECT content_key, (mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Episode_Total')::int AS episode_count, (mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Seasons_Total')::int AS season_count, CASE WHEN (mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Seasons_Total')::int > 0 THEN ROUND(((mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Episode_Total')::float / (mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Seasons_Total')::float)::numeric, 2) ELSE NULL END AS season_to_episode_ratio FROM content_info WHERE TRIM(mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Episode_Total') ~ '^[0-9]+$' AND TRIM(mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Seasons_Total') ~ '^[0-9]+$') SELECT content_key, episode_count, season_count, season_to_episode_ratio FROM episode_ratio_calc WHERE season_to_episode_ratio IS NOT NULL ORDER BY season_to_episode_ratio DESC;

question: Let’s figure out what the most frequent top-end maturity rating is across all the shows. Basically, I want to scan all the records, grab the maturity info, and tell me which of those high-end ratings pops up the most. Just return the one that shows up the most often.
gold_sql: WITH raw AS (SELECT TRIM(ratinginfo->>'Peak_Rating') AS rating FROM show_rollups WHERE TRIM(ratinginfo->>'Peak_Rating') IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(ratinginfo->>'Peak_Rating') <> ''), norm AS (SELECT rating, UPPER(REGEXP_REPLACE(rating, '[^A-Za-z0-9]+', '', 'g')) AS base FROM raw), cleaned AS (SELECT CASE WHEN base ~ '^(TV)?Y7FV$' THEN 'TV-Y7-FV' WHEN base ~ '^(TV)?Y7$' THEN 'TV-Y7' WHEN base ~ '^(TV)?Y$' THEN 'TV-Y' WHEN base ~ '^(TV)?G$' THEN 'TV-G' WHEN base ~ '^(TV)?PG$' OR base='PARENTALGUIDANCE' THEN 'TV-PG' WHEN base ~ '^(TV)?14$' OR base='T14' OR base='FOURTEEN' THEN 'TV-14' WHEN base ~ '^(TV)?MA$' OR base='MATURE' THEN 'TV-MA' WHEN base IN ('NR','UNRATED','UR') THEN 'NR' ELSE UPPER(TRIM(rating)) END AS normalized_rating FROM norm), counts AS (SELECT normalized_rating, COUNT(*) AS freq FROM cleaned GROUP BY normalized_rating) SELECT normalized_rating AS most_common_peak_rating FROM counts ORDER BY freq DESC LIMIT 1;

question: Which franchises are producing the most content? Group shows in the same franchise and add up their episodes. Some episode counts may be text or invalid — after trimming whitespace, parse only digit strings (digits 0–9 only) and treat the rest as zero. Show only franchises with more than 100 total episodes, listing the identifier, number of shows, and total episodes from largest to smallest.
gold_sql: WITH franchise_summary AS ( SELECT c.series_id, COUNT(*) AS total_shows, SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(ci.mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Episode_Total') ~ '^[0-9]+$' THEN (TRIM(ci.mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Episode_Total'))::int ELSE 0 END) AS total_episodes FROM core c JOIN content_info ci ON c.content_key = ci.content_key WHERE c.series_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.series_id ) SELECT series_id, total_shows, total_episodes FROM franchise_summary WHERE total_episodes > 100 ORDER BY total_episodes DESC, series_id;

question: Let’s see how our shows are spread out across the different subscription plans. For each plan, I want to know how many titles it has and what chunk of the full catalog that is. Just give me the plan name, the total count of media in it, and what percentage of the catalog that represents. Start with the plans that have the biggest share of content.
gold_sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT sr.srlinks AS tier_key, sr.srkeys AS content_key
  FROM show_rollups sr
),
per_content_media AS (
  SELECT
    b.tier_key,
    b.content_key,
    CASE
      WHEN TRIM(ci.mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Videos_Total') ~ '^\d+$'
        THEN (ci.mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Videos_Total')::bigint
      ELSE 0
    END AS videos_total
  FROM base b
  JOIN content_info ci ON ci.content_key = b.content_key
),
tier_media_totals AS (
  SELECT tier_key, SUM(videos_total) AS media_total
  FROM per_content_media
  GROUP BY tier_key
),
total_sum AS (
  SELECT SUM(media_total) AS grand_total FROM tier_media_totals
)
SELECT
  t.tier_key,
  r.tiertype,
  t.media_total,
  ROUND(t.media_total * 1.0 / NULLIF(ts.grand_total, 0), 4) AS tier_distribution_ratio
FROM tier_media_totals t
JOIN rollups r ON r.tierkey = t.tier_key
CROSS JOIN total_sum ts
ORDER BY tier_distribution_ratio DESC;

question: Let’s see which franchises are really making waves across different subscription levels. We’re looking for those that have at least 3 shows, and those shows appear across 3 or more tiers. For each of these franchise powerhouses, show me the franchise ID, how many shows they’ve got, and how many tiers they show up in. Sort the list by number of shows to spotlight the most widely spread ones first.
gold_sql:
WITH franchise_shows AS (
  SELECT
    c.series_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.content_key) AS show_count
  FROM core c
  WHERE c.series_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY c.series_id
),
franchise_tiers AS (
  SELECT
    c.series_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT sr.srlinks) AS tier_count
  FROM core c
  JOIN show_rollups sr
    ON sr.srkeys = c.content_key
  WHERE c.series_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY c.series_id
)
SELECT
  fs.series_id AS franchise_id,
  fs.show_count,
  ft.tier_count
FROM franchise_shows fs
JOIN franchise_tiers ft
  ON ft.series_id = fs.series_id
WHERE fs.show_count >= 3
  AND ft.tier_count >= 3
ORDER BY fs.show_count DESC;

question: Let’s dive into the main genre types that keep popping up in our show catalog. I’m only interested in shows labeled as Drama, Comedy, or Animation and Cartoons. For each of those, can you pull together a quick list that includes the show’s ID, its title, and what genre it’s tagged under? Sort the list by title.
gold_sql: SELECT c.content_key, c.content_title, c.genreclass->>'Primary_Genre' AS primary_genre FROM core c WHERE c.genreclass->>'Primary_Genre' IN ('Drama', 'Comedy', 'Animation and Cartoons') ORDER BY c.content_title;

question: I want to look at how packed each show’s video library is. Can you pull up a list that shows the total number of video items for each show and group them into three levels? Label them High if they’ve got over 500 videos, Medium if they’re between 200 and 500, and Low if they’re under 200. Let’s sort the list so the shows with the most content show up first, and include the show ID, total count, and the volume level tag.
gold_sql: WITH content_volume_classification AS ( SELECT ci.content_key, (ci.mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Videos_Total')::int AS total_video_volume, CASE WHEN (ci.mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Videos_Total')::int > 500 THEN 'High' WHEN (ci.mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Videos_Total')::int BETWEEN 200 AND 500 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END AS volume_level FROM content_info ci WHERE (ci.mediacounts->'content_volumes'->>'Videos_Total') IS NOT NULL ) SELECT content_key, total_video_volume, volume_level FROM content_volume_classification ORDER BY total_video_volume DESC;

question: Which show feels the most crammed with promotional stuff? Just give me the one with the heaviest promo presence overall.
gold_sql: SELECT MAX(((CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(tiernotices->'free_tier'->>'Alert_Note'), '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(tiernotices->'free_tier'->>'Avail_Note'), '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(tiernotices->'free_tier'->>'Promo_Note'), '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(tiernotices->'free_tier'->>'Expire_Note'), '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(tiernotices->'member_tier'->>'Alert_Note'), '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(tiernotices->'member_tier'->>'Avail_Note'), '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(tiernotices->'member_tier'->>'Promo_Note'), '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(tiernotices->'member_tier'->>'Expire_Note'), '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) / 8.0) AS max_promo_saturation_ratio FROM promo_info;

question: How many shows land in our usual user-score buckets—Low, Medium, or High? Just give me the total.
gold_sql: WITH standard_score_ranges AS (  SELECT 'Low' AS tier, 0.0 AS min_score, 2.0 AS max_exclusive, false AS include_max UNION ALL  SELECT 'Medium',        2.0,             4.0,               false UNION ALL  SELECT 'High',          4.0,             5.0,               true ), scores AS (  SELECT     c.content_key,     NULLIF(       substring(COALESCE(c.genreclass->>'User_Score',                          c.genreclass->>'userscore',                          c.genreclass->>'user_score','')                 FROM '([0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)'),       ''     )::float AS raw_score   FROM core c ), bounded AS (  SELECT content_key,          CASE WHEN raw_score BETWEEN 0 AND 5 THEN raw_score END AS score   FROM scores ) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT b.content_key) AS shows_with_matched_score_range FROM bounded b JOIN standard_score_ranges r   ON b.score >= r.min_score  AND (b.score < r.max_exclusive OR (r.include_max AND b.score <= r.max_exclusive));

question: I want to find shows that show up in three or more different subscription tiers. For each show, can you count how many unique tiers it’s available in? First, keep the ones that are in at least three tiers, and then sort the results from the most widely distributed to the last.
gold_sql: WITH tier_counts AS (     SELECT         srkeys AS content_key,         COUNT(DISTINCT r.tiertype) AS tier_count     FROM show_rollups s     JOIN rollups r       ON s.srlinks = r.tierkey     GROUP BY srkeys ) SELECT     c.content_key,     t.tier_count FROM tier_counts t JOIN core c   ON t.content_key = c.content_key WHERE t.tier_count >= 3 ORDER BY t.tier_count DESC;

question: Let’s grab the shows where the bigger of their trailer or feature count is over 100. Show the ID, title, and that number, sorted from highest to lowest.
gold_sql: WITH show_rollups AS (   SELECT * FROM (     VALUES       ('SH001', '{"standard_content": {"Feature_Vol": "120", "Trailer_Vol": "95"}}'::jsonb),       ('SH002', '{"standard_content": {"Feature_Vol": "60",  "Trailer_Vol": "130"}}'::jsonb),       ('SH003', '{"standard_content": {"Feature_Vol": "99",  "Trailer_Vol": "98"}}'::jsonb),       ('SH004', '{"standard_content": {"Feature_Vol": "",    "Trailer_Vol": "200"}}'::jsonb),       ('SH005', '{"standard_content": {"Feature_Vol": "150", "Trailer_Vol": ""}}'::jsonb)   ) AS t(srkeys, contentvols) ), core AS (   SELECT * FROM (     VALUES       ('SH001', 'Galaxy Showdown', 'COMP01'),       ('SH002', 'Ocean Deep',      'COMP02'),       ('SH003', 'Lost in Code',    'COMP03'),       ('SH004', 'Shadow War',      'COMP04'),       ('SH005', 'Quiet Forest',    'COMP05')   ) AS t(content_key, content_title, studiolink) ), media_volumes AS (   SELECT     sr.srkeys AS content_key,     c.content_title,     COALESCE(NULLIF(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Feature_Vol','')::int, 0) AS feature_vol,     COALESCE(NULLIF(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Trailer_Vol','')::int, 0) AS trailer_vol,     GREATEST(       COALESCE(NULLIF(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Feature_Vol','')::int, 0),       COALESCE(NULLIF(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'Trailer_Vol','')::int, 0)     ) AS peak_media_volume   FROM show_rollups sr   JOIN core c ON sr.srkeys = c.content_key ) SELECT   mv.content_key,   mv.content_title,   mv.peak_media_volume FROM media_volumes mv WHERE mv.peak_media_volume > 100 ORDER BY mv.peak_media_volume DESC;

question: I want to see how shows rank based on what viewers think. Just group them by how well they’re rated, ignore anything without a proper score, and tell me the show ID, name, how it scored, and which group it ended up in—start from the highest-rated and go down.
gold_sql: WITH rating_data AS (   SELECT     c.content_key,     c.content_title,     CAST(       NULLIF(         REGEXP_REPLACE(           COALESCE(             c.genreclass ->> 'User_Score',             c.genreclass ->> 'userscore',             c.genreclass ->> 'user_score',             ''           ),           '[^0-9\.]',           '',           'g'         ),         ''       ) AS FLOAT     ) AS userscore   FROM core c ), banded AS (   SELECT     content_key,     content_title,     userscore,     CASE       WHEN userscore < 3.5 THEN 'Low'       WHEN userscore <= 4.2 THEN 'Medium'       ELSE 'High'     END AS rating_band   FROM rating_data   WHERE userscore IS NOT NULL ) SELECT content_key, content_title, userscore, rating_band FROM banded ORDER BY userscore DESC;

question: Which shows actually have film clips? List the ones with the most film-related clips first. For each show, show the title, how many film clips it has, and a quick flag for Has Clips or No Clips.
gold_sql:
WITH clip_check AS (
  SELECT
    sr.srkeys AS content_key,
    c.content_title,
    CAST(NULLIF(BTRIM(sr.contentvols->'standard_content'->>'FilmClip_Vol'), '') AS INT) AS film_clip_vol
  FROM show_rollups sr
  JOIN core c ON sr.srkeys = c.content_key
),
clip_per_show AS (
  -- If a show appears in multiple tiers, take the maximum film-clip count once per show
  SELECT content_key, MAX(film_clip_vol) AS film_clip_vol
  FROM clip_check
  GROUP BY content_key
),
flagged AS (
  SELECT
    cps.content_key,
    c.content_title,
    cps.film_clip_vol,
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(cps.film_clip_vol, 0) > 0 THEN 'Has Clips' ELSE 'No Clips' END AS clip_flag
  FROM clip_per_show cps
  JOIN core c ON cps.content_key = c.content_key
)
SELECT content_key, content_title, film_clip_vol, clip_flag
FROM flagged
ORDER BY film_clip_vol DESC NULLS LAST;

question: Let’s see which shows are loading up on promo messages. For each one, count availability updates, promo messages, alerts, and expiration notices across the free and member tiers. Only include shows with at least one note, and list them starting with the most.
gold_sql: WITH notes AS (   SELECT     p.content_key,     (       (CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(p.tiernotices->'free_tier'->>'Avail_Note'),  '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) +       (CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(p.tiernotices->'free_tier'->>'Promo_Note'),  '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) +       (CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(p.tiernotices->'free_tier'->>'Alert_Note'),  '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) +       (CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(p.tiernotices->'free_tier'->>'Expire_Note'), '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) +       (CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(p.tiernotices->'member_tier'->>'Avail_Note'),  '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) +       (CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(p.tiernotices->'member_tier'->>'Promo_Note'),  '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) +       (CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(p.tiernotices->'member_tier'->>'Alert_Note'),  '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) +       (CASE WHEN NULLIF(BTRIM(p.tiernotices->'member_tier'->>'Expire_Note'), '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)     ) AS total_promo_notes   FROM promo_info p ), final AS (   SELECT content_key, total_promo_notes   FROM notes   WHERE total_promo_notes > 0 ) SELECT content_key, total_promo_notes FROM final ORDER BY total_promo_notes DESC, content_key;

question: Give me all platforms sorted by its risk score, most dangerous on top and show 4 digits.
gold_sql:
SELECT m."PlatCode",
       ROUND(
         (0.4*(m.platform_compliance->>'vuln_inst_count')::numeric +
          0.3*(m.platform_compliance->>'sec_event_count')::numeric +
          0.3*COALESCE(NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(m."RepScore",'[^0-9.]','','g'), '')::numeric,0))/100
       ,4) AS mrs
FROM markets m
ORDER BY mrs DESC;

question: Split shoppers into three risk-per-dollar groups; for each group, show how many shoppers there are, what fraction of their orders go across countries, and how often their sessions look highly/medium/low hidden.
gold_sql: WITH brdr AS (SELECT b."AcqCode" AS buyer_id,NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(b."buyer_risk_profile"->>'risk_dollar_ratio','[^0-9.]','','g'),'')::numeric AS brdr FROM buyers b),th AS (SELECT percentile_disc(0.3333) WITHIN GROUP(ORDER BY brdr) AS p1,percentile_disc(0.6667) WITHIN GROUP(ORDER BY brdr) AS p2 FROM brdr WHERE brdr IS NOT NULL),bucketed_buyers AS (SELECT br.buyer_id,CASE WHEN br.brdr IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN br.brdr<=th.p1 THEN 'Low' WHEN br.brdr<=th.p2 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'High' END AS risk_bucket FROM brdr br CROSS JOIN th),buyer_set AS (SELECT buyer_id,risk_bucket FROM bucketed_buyers WHERE risk_bucket IS NOT NULL),tx AS (SELECT bs.risk_bucket,t."EventCode" AS event_code,LOWER(COALESCE(t."CrossBorder"::text,'')) IN('true','t','1','yes','y') AS is_cross_border FROM buyer_set bs JOIN transactions t ON t."AcqLink"=bs.buyer_id),sess AS (SELECT tx.risk_bucket,tx.event_code,LOWER(cs."AnonLevel") AS anon_level FROM tx LEFT JOIN connection_security cs ON cs."TxnPointer"=tx.event_code),buyers_agg AS (SELECT risk_bucket,COUNT(DISTINCT buyer_id) AS buyer_count FROM buyer_set GROUP BY risk_bucket),tx_agg AS (SELECT risk_bucket,COUNT(DISTINCT event_code) AS txn_count,COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN is_cross_border THEN event_code END) AS cross_border_txn_count FROM tx GROUP BY risk_bucket),sess_agg AS (SELECT risk_bucket,COUNT(DISTINCT event_code) AS sess_count,COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN anon_level='high' THEN event_code END) AS anon_high_sessions,COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN anon_level='medium' THEN event_code END) AS anon_medium_sessions,COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN anon_level='low' THEN event_code END) AS anon_low_sessions FROM sess GROUP BY risk_bucket) SELECT b.risk_bucket,b.buyer_count,COALESCE(t.txn_count,0) AS question: How reliable are our scan alignments? For each alignment record, could you show me the registration accuracy relative to scan resolution and the registration confidence category. I need to see its registration ID, project ID, accuracy measurements, error values, calculated ratio, and the confidence category.
gold_sql: SELECT r.logregistry AS registration_id, r.arcref AS project_id, COALESCE((r.reg_accuracy->>'Log_Accu_Mm')::real, 1.0) AS registration_accuracy_mm, COALESCE((r.reg_accuracy->>'Err_Val_Mm')::real, 1.0) AS error_value_mm, ROUND((COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Scan_Resol_Mm')::real, 1.0) / (COALESCE((r.reg_accuracy->>'Log_Accu_Mm')::real, 1.0) * SQRT(1.0 + COALESCE((r.reg_accuracy->>'Err_Val_Mm')::real, 1.0) / COALESCE((r.reg_accuracy->>'Log_Accu_Mm')::real, 1.0))))::numeric, 2) AS rar, CASE WHEN (COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Scan_Resol_Mm')::real, 1.0) / (COALESCE((r.reg_accuracy->>'Log_Accu_Mm')::real, 1.0) * SQRT(1.0 + COALESCE((r.reg_accuracy->>'Err_Val_Mm')::real, 1.0) / COALESCE((r.reg_accuracy->>'Log_Accu_Mm')::real, 1.0)))) > 1.5 AND COALESCE(r.reg_accuracy->>'Log_Method', '') ILIKE '%Target%' THEN 'High Confidence' WHEN (COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Scan_Resol_Mm')::real, 1.0) / (COALESCE((r.reg_accuracy->>'Log_Accu_Mm')::real, 1.0) * SQRT(1.0 + COALESCE((r.reg_accuracy->>'Err_Val_Mm')::real, 1.0) / COALESCE((r.reg_accuracy->>'Log_Accu_Mm')::real, 1.0)))) BETWEEN 1.0 AND 1.5 THEN 'Medium Confidence' ELSE 'Low Confidence' END AS confidence_level FROM registration r JOIN pointcloud pc ON r.arcref = pc.arcref AND r.crewref = pc.crewref WHERE r.reg_accuracy IS NOT NULL AND pc.cloud_metrics IS NOT NULL ORDER BY rar DESC;

question: Which archaeologicalsites have the best digital preservation? Rank our locations showing their ID, designation, and a comprehensive metric for evaluating digital preservation quality, with the best first.
gold_sql:
WITH adc_data AS (
    SELECT
        s.zoneref,
        AVG(
            -- SQS calculation: (10/SRI)^1.5 * (SCE/100) * (1 - noise/30)^2 * 0.4
            (POWER(10.0 / (
                ln(COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Scan_Resol_Mm')::real, 1.0) * 1000.0) / 
                ln(COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Point_Dense')::bigint, 1000)::real) * 5.0
            ), 1.5) *
            (COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Cover_Pct')::real, 0.0) * 
             (1 + COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Lap_Pct')::real, 0.0) / 100.0 * 
              (1 - COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Cover_Pct')::real, 0.0) / 100.0)) / 100.0) *
            POWER(GREATEST(0.0, 1.0 - COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Noise_Db')::real, 0.0) / 30.0), 2) * 0.4)
            + 
            -- MFS calculation: MCR * (TDI/10) * (1 + exp(-geom_accuracy))
            (COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Faces')::bigint, 0)::real / 
             GREATEST(1.0, COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Verts')::bigint, 1)::real * 
                     POWER(COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Res_Mm')::real, 1.0), 2)) * 1000.0 *
             (COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Tex_Pix')::bigint, 1024)::real / 
              GREATEST(1.0, sqrt(COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Faces')::bigint, 1)::real) * 
                      COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Res_Mm')::real, 1.0)) * 0.01 *0.1) *
             (1 + exp(-COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Geom_Delta_Mm')::real, 1.0))) * 0.4)
            + 
            -- SCE calculation: Coverage * (1 + overlap/100 * (1 - coverage/100)) * 0.2
            (COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Cover_Pct')::real, 0.0) * 
             (1 + COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Lap_Pct')::real, 0.0) / 100.0 * 
              (1 - COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Cover_Pct')::real, 0.0) / 100.0)) * 0.2)
            - 
            -- Noise penalty: 5 * sqrt(noise/10)
            (5.0 * sqrt(GREATEST(0.0, COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Noise_Db')::real, 0.0) / 10.0)))
        ) AS adc
    FROM scans s
    JOIN pointcloud pc ON s.arcref = pc.arcref
    LEFT JOIN mesh m ON s.zoneref = m.zoneref
    WHERE pc.cloud_metrics IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY s.zoneref
),
mfs_data AS (
    SELECT
        m.zoneref,
        AVG(
            -- MCR * (TDI/10) * (1 + exp(-geometric_accuracy))
            COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Faces')::bigint, 0)::real / 
            GREATEST(1.0, COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Verts')::bigint, 1)::real * 
                    POWER(COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Res_Mm')::real, 1.0), 2)) * 1000.0 *
            (COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Tex_Pix')::bigint, 1024)::real / 
             GREATEST(1.0, sqrt(COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Faces')::bigint, 1)::real) * 
                     COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Res_Mm')::real, 1.0)) * 0.01 * 0.1) *
            (1 + exp(-COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Geom_Delta_Mm')::real, 1.0)))
        ) AS mfs
    FROM mesh m
    WHERE m.mesh_specs IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY m.zoneref
),
rar_data AS (
    SELECT
        s.zoneref,
        AVG(
            -- RAR = scan_resolution / (registration_accuracy * sqrt(1 + error_val/registration_accuracy))
            COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Scan_Resol_Mm')::real, 1.0) / 
            GREATEST(0.001, COALESCE((r.reg_accuracy->>'Log_Accu_Mm')::real, 1.0) * 
                    sqrt(1.0 + GREATEST(0.0, COALESCE((r.reg_accuracy->>'Err_Val_Mm')::real, 0.0) / 
                                        GREATEST(0.001, COALESCE((r.reg_accuracy->>'Log_Accu_Mm')::real, 1.0)))))
        ) AS rar
    FROM registration r
    JOIN scans s ON r.arcref = s.arcref
    JOIN pointcloud pc ON r.arcref = pc.arcref
    WHERE r.reg_accuracy IS NOT NULL 
      AND pc.cloud_metrics IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY s.zoneref
),
sce_data AS (
    SELECT
        s.zoneref,
        AVG(
            -- SCE = coverage * (1 + overlap/100 * (1 - coverage/100))
            COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Cover_Pct')::real, 0.0) * 
            (1 + COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Lap_Pct')::real, 0.0) / 100.0 * 
             (1 - COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Cover_Pct')::real, 0.0) / 100.0))
        ) AS sce
    FROM scans s
    JOIN pointcloud pc ON s.arcref = pc.arcref
    WHERE pc.cloud_metrics IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY s.zoneref
),
err_data AS (
    SELECT
        s.zoneref,
        AVG(
            -- Error ratio for penalty calculation
            COALESCE((r.reg_accuracy->>'Err_Val_Mm')::real, 0.0) / 
            GREATEST(0.001, COALESCE((pc.cloud_metrics->>'Scan_Resol_Mm')::real, 1.0))
        ) AS error_ratio
    FROM registration r
    JOIN scans s ON r.arcref = s.arcref
    JOIN pointcloud pc ON r.arcref = pc.arcref
    WHERE r.reg_accuracy IS NOT NULL 
      AND pc.cloud_metrics IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY s.zoneref
)
SELECT
    st.zoneregistry AS site_code,
    st.zonelabel AS site_name,
    ROUND(CAST(
        (0.3 * COALESCE(adc.adc, 0.0)) +
        (0.3 * COALESCE(mfs.mfs, 0.0)) +
        (0.2 * COALESCE(rar.rar, 0.0)) +
        (0.2 * COALESCE(sce.sce, 0.0)) -
        (2.0 * sqrt(GREATEST(0.0, COALESCE(err.error_ratio, 0.0))))
    AS NUMERIC), 2) AS dpq
FROM sites st
LEFT JOIN adc_data adc ON st.zoneregistry = adc.zoneref
LEFT JOIN mfs_data mfs ON st.zoneregistry = mfs.zoneref
LEFT JOIN rar_data rar ON st.zoneregistry = rar.zoneref
LEFT JOIN sce_data sce ON st.zoneregistry = sce.zoneref
LEFT JOIN err_data err ON st.zoneregistry = err.zoneref
ORDER BY dpq DESC;

question: How good are our 3D models based on the criteria for high-fidelity standard? Please generate a comprehensive report that shows each site's ID, name, total mesh count, high-fidelity mesh count and proportion (as a percentage), average ratio of mesh complexity, average resolution parameters (in mm), average geometric accuracy measurements and Mesh Quality category. Present the data with the highest-fidelity results first.
gold_sql:
WITH mesh_analysis AS (
    SELECT 
        m.zoneref AS site_code,
        m.facetregistry AS mesh_id,
        -- MCR calculation with proper NULL handling and division protection
        COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Faces')::bigint, 0)::real / 
        GREATEST(1.0, 
            COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Verts')::bigint, 1)::real * 
            POWER(COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Res_Mm')::real, 1.0), 2)
        ) * 1000.0 AS mcr,
        COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Res_Mm')::real, 0.0) AS facet_res_mm,
        COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Geom_Delta_Mm')::real, 0.0) AS geom_delta_mm,
        -- High Fidelity Mesh criteria: MCR > 5.0, Resolution < 1.0mm, Geometric Accuracy < 0.5mm
        CASE 
            WHEN (COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Faces')::bigint, 0)::real / 
                  GREATEST(1.0, 
                      COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Verts')::bigint, 1)::real * 
                      POWER(COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Res_Mm')::real, 1.0), 2)
                  ) * 1000.0) > 5.0 
                 AND COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Res_Mm')::real, 999.0) < 1.0 
                 AND COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Geom_Delta_Mm')::real, 999.0) < 0.5 
            THEN TRUE
            ELSE FALSE
        END AS is_high_fidelity
    FROM mesh m
    WHERE m.mesh_specs IS NOT NULL
      AND COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Verts')::bigint, 0) > 0
      AND COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Faces')::bigint, 0) > 0
      AND COALESCE((m.mesh_specs->>'Facet_Res_Mm')::real, 0.0) > 0.0
)
SELECT 
    s.zoneregistry AS site_code,
    s.zonelabel AS site_name,
    COALESCE(COUNT(ma.mesh_id), 0) AS total_meshes,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN ma.is_high_fidelity THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS high_fidelity_count,
    CASE 
        WHEN COUNT(ma.mesh_id) = 0 THEN 0.00
        ELSE ROUND(
            (SUM(CASE WHEN ma.is_high_fidelity THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)::numeric / 
             COUNT(ma.mesh_id)::numeric * 100.0), 2
        )
    END AS high_fidelity_percentage,
    CASE 
        WHEN COUNT(ma.mesh_id) = 0 THEN NULL
        ELSE ROUND(AVG(ma.mcr)::numeric, 2)
    END AS avg_mcr,
    CASE 
        WHEN COUNT(ma.mesh_id) = 0 THEN NULL
        ELSE ROUND(AVG(ma.facet_res_mm)::numeric, 2)
    END AS avg_mesh_resolution_mm,
    CASE 
        WHEN COUNT(ma.mesh_id) = 0 THEN NULL
        ELSE ROUND(AVG(ma.geom_delta_mm)::numeric, 2)
    END AS avg_geometric_accuracy_mm,
    -- Mesh Quality Classification based on knowledge bank #53
    CASE 
        WHEN COUNT(ma.mesh_id) = 0 THEN 'No Mesh Data'
        WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN ma.is_high_fidelity THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Has High-Fidelity Meshes'
        ELSE 'Standard Mesh Quality'
    END AS mesh_quality_classification
FROM sites s
LEFT JOIN mesh_analysis ma ON s.zoneregistry = ma.site_code
GROUP BY s.zoneregistry, s.zonelabel
ORDER BY 
    high_fidelity_percentage DESC, 
    high_fidelity_count DESC,
    total_meshes DESC;
